title: Overselling Is an Integration Problem, Not a Warehouse One
summary: Bring Amazon Seller Central data into NetSuite reconciliation with stable marketplace and order identifiers. The native Amazon connector is read-only;…
body_markdown:
Amazon and NetSuite answer different operational questions. Amazon identifies the marketplace order and reports its channel state. NetSuite holds the ERP records your team uses for fulfillment, purchasing, and finance. The useful integration begins by relating those records without confusing visibility with permission to change either system.


The[Stacksync Amazon Seller Central connector documentation](https://docs.stacksync.com/two-way-sync/connectors/amazon-seller-central) specifies read-only synchronization from Amazon to destination systems, with historical and incremental synchronization of supported objects and reports. The native connector does not provide a NetSuite-to-Amazon write path. Updating listings, publishing available-to-promise quantities, issuing refunds, or confirming shipments in Amazon requires a separately supported outbound integration.


## Start with the records you can actually read


Inventory the objects and reports available to the authorized Amazon account before choosing the operating workflow. A connector name is not evidence that every account exposes every report, that a report is current enough for a dispatch decision, or that a corresponding NetSuite record can be written. Confirm those details against the selected entities, permissions, and account configuration.


Business question Reference to preserve Validation before use


Which channel order is this? Seller account, marketplace, Amazon order ID, and line ID Confirm the selected source exposes the identifiers and statuses required by the reconciliation.


Which ERP record represents it? NetSuite customer, item, order, and external reference Approve item matching and destination write operations before creating or changing ERP records.


Is the physical unit available? Fulfillment channel, SKU, location, observation time, and quantity definition Keep Amazon-held stock separate from merchant-held stock and quantities already committed elsewhere.


Why does the financial amount differ? Order reference, report period, currency, fee or adjustment reference Verify report coverage and timing before treating an unmatched amount as a finance error.


## Keep channel evidence and ERP decisions separate


A seller-fulfilled order and an FBA order should not follow an identical inventory assumption. Determine where the goods physically reside and which operational record establishes their status. Do not add Amazon-held quantities to warehouse quantities merely because the SKU is the same. Do not treat a report observation as a reservation or shipment commitment.


Preserve source values alongside the matched ERP reference and the time each was observed. An operations analyst should be able to distinguish an Amazon cancellation from an ERP picking status, and then decide which work must pause. Copying one status over the other can erase the very disagreement the team needs to investigate.


## Build one reconciliation case per business discrepancy


Begin with a small sample spanning marketplaces, fulfillment channels, partial orders, and amended records. Match the source line to its approved ERP counterpart. When no match exists, expose the missing relationship for review rather than guessing from the product name or silently creating another order.


Give the case a stable reference derived from the source identity and the discrepancy being investigated. Reprocessing the same source observation should update that case, not create another task or duplicate financial effect. Keep the original observations so a reviewer can explain why the case was opened and what changed before it was closed.


For financial reconciliation, compare like periods and currencies and retain the report reference supporting each proposed explanation. A payout, an order total, and net revenue after fees answer different questions. Missing or delayed source evidence belongs in a waiting state; it is not permission to issue a credit or post an adjustment.


## Evaluate outbound Amazon actions as a separate integration


A business may also need to publish inventory, change a listing, or confirm a seller-fulfilled shipment. Those are separate outbound requirements. Identify the authorized integration that can perform each operation, its supported API action, owner, retry behavior, and reconciliation record. The native read-only Amazon connector does not fulfill those requirements.


Keep the two workstreams visible in the design review: source-data ingestion supplies evidence; an independently verified outbound process performs a permitted change. If that outbound process is unavailable, the workflow should route the task to the responsible operator. It must not report that Amazon was updated because NetSuite changed.
